item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1R52K9CONmo

值得閱讀的理由

  • 瞭解 vivo 最新旗艦 X500 Pro Max 在電池容量與台積電先進製程晶片上的重大規格升級。
  • 掌握首發 Sony LYT-910 感光元件與 17EV 超高動態範圍技術，如何大幅提升影像拍攝品質。
  • 探索全新專業攝影套裝配件、長焦鏡頭下放實力，以及周杰倫聯名「晴天」濾鏡的豐富玩法。

摘要

全新旗艦定位與周杰倫聯名亮點

作者開箱並介紹了 vivo 最新推出的年度旗艦機 vivo X500 Pro Max。本代旗艦最大的話題之一是邀請到 周杰倫 擔任品牌代言人，全系列特別內建了聯名款「晴天」濾鏡以致敬經典 MV 氛圍。核心規格方面，手機搭載採用台積電最新 N2P 製程的天璣 96 Pro 旗艦處理器，電池容量更大幅提升至領先業界的 7,800 mAh，並搭配 90W 有線與 40W 無線快充。

革命性影像規格與專業長焦套裝

影像系統是該機的最大亮點，作者特別點出多項業界領先配置。主鏡頭採用 vivo 與 Sony 聯合研發的 1/1.28 吋 5,000 萬畫素 Sony LYT-910 感光元件，並導入 LOFIC 技術，具備真實 17EV 超高動態範圍，帶來相較一般手機多達 32 倍的動態範圍躍升，並輔以 3 軸 OIS 頂級防手震規格。長焦端則配備 2 億畫素大底潛望鏡頭，並首次下放支援 400mm G2 Ultra 望遠鏡頭 與專業攝影套裝，讓該機無需直上 Ultra 型號就能化身最強「演唱會神器」。

質感外觀設計與多元智慧拍照功能

在機身外觀上，作者展示了兼具極簡與細節的「星光灰」配色，背蓋採用具備潮汐起伏微曲弧度的冷雕雙工藝玻璃，支援 IP68 與 IP69 最高防塵防水等級、紅外線遙控以及實體雙卡搭配 eSIM。鏡頭模組旁還隱藏了 1536 測距點的多區雷射對焦感測器以確保穩定對焦。在拍攝體驗上，相機整合了人像、風景與舞台等情境的 AI 自動優化模式，並首創支援高達 8K 動態照片（Live Photos） 與獨特的鏡頭除霧功能，提供全面且豐富的創作樂趣。

================================================

In my hand is the newly released flagship from vivo, the X500 Pro Max. Hi, welcome back. I'm 2027. The new round of flagship smartphone wars has been heating up since October, and right here in my hand is the latest annual flagship from vivo: the X500 Pro Max. The big news this year is that vivo actually got Jay Chou as their brand ambassador. You'll notice not only is he featured in all the early promotional materials, but in the entire X500 series. , vivo has included a co-branded "Sunny Day" filter, recreating the aesthetic of that classic MV, which we'll take a closer look at later. Getting back to it , the vivo X500 Pro Max flagship has all the specs you'd expect, including the new-generation Dimensity 96 Pro flagship processor built on TSMC's latest N2P process. The highlight is that the battery capacity in this international version has been significantly upgraded from the previous generation's 6,510 mAh. to an industry-leading 7,800 mAh, paired with 90W wired and 40W wireless fast charging. However, for those of you watching this for vivo, I’m sure you’re most interested in the camera. Although this year’s X500 Pro Max might look similar to the previous generation on the spec sheet. In reality, the underlying hardware has received a massive overhaul, with many first-time features, especially in imaging. For example, the first industry-first is the new 1/1.28-inch 50-megapixel large sensor co-developed by vivo and Sony. It. utilizes the Sony LYT-L 910 flagship sensor, which features the latest LOFIC technology. With vivo's tuning and the support of LOFIC technology, the X500 Pro Max's main lens can achieve a real 17-stop ultra-high dynamic range. As we’ve shared before, most current smartphones hover around 12EV, and even the previous generation X300 Pro only reached 14EV. So, the 17EV achieved by this LYT-L 910 is 2 to the power of 5 compared to standard 12EV phones, representing a 32-fold improvement. Even. compared to the 14EV of the previous X300 Pro, this generation offers a 2 to the power of 3 improvement, which is an 8-fold increase. According to vivo, the 17EV they claim is a true 17 stops; if using the peak values often cited for marketing, the X500 Pro Max can reach up to 18.4 EV. On top of that, this main lens is also equipped with 3-axis OIS stabilization hardware, achieving a C.0 -level top-tier stabilization spec. Moving past the main lens, let’s look at. the second industry-first: vivo and Samsung have co-launched the new-generation HP0 large-sensor telephoto lens. While it maintains the 1 /1.4-inch 200-megapixel large sensor hardware, it also achieves the C.0- level stabilization spec and adopts a 1 + 5 glass lens design. But the real highlight is this box you see on my table. That's right, today we're unboxing Vivo's top-tier ETB Photography Master Set. Beyond the stylish silver dedicated case, the magnification adapter ring on. it, and the professional photography grip—accessories you're already familiar with—this year's X500 Pro Max directly supports the 200mm Vivo G2 lipstick telephoto lens, as well as the 400mm G2 Ultra telephoto lens, which has been trickled down from the X300 Ultra for the first time. This is also the first time the Pro series has supported the G2 Ultra, letting you turn it into Vivo's best concert-shooting device without needing to step up to the Ultra model. We'll get to that later. By the way,.

this set also includes a strap and two lens rings with different designs that you can swap based on your preference. Finally, seeing the classic ZEISS blue logo on the case, the lens, and the phone itself confirms that the X500 Pro Max continues the deep collaboration between Vivo and ZEISS. Alright, I've talked a bit too much in the intro. As I'm testing this now, I don't know the actual retail price or the version coming to Taiwan yet—you guys can let me know in the comments. Anyway, how does the Vivo X500 Pro Max actually perform? Let's take a look together. Let's start by looking at the exterior. I personally think this year's Vivo X500 Pro Max has become much more refined compared to the simplicity of the previous generation. First, the version we have here is my favorite this year, Starry Gray. From the front, it’s a gray-toned phone with a minimalist design and a high-quality feel. But when you catch it in the light, you. can see the cold-sculpted glass features two sections with different finishes spliced together. Look closer, and you'll see sparkles across the body, just like stars twinkling in the night sky. I actually quite like the name announced at the launch, "Earth Gray," which is very evocative. Besides that, if you look closely at the seam where the sections meet. That's right, the top section is slightly raised. Vivo has cleverly created a curved design on this cold-sculpted glass, inspired by the changing tides. Also, compared to the last generation,. this year’s lens ring features a larger area of dense texturing. Around the Oreo module, there's an added gray border in a matching color. Contrasting with the simplicity of the previous generation, I really like this year's design. By the way, the X500 Pro Max also retains the shortcut button design. So you can do things like long-press to open the camera or double-press to turn on the flashlight; it's a very useful setting. Finally, there are three more points regarding the exterior. First, the X500 Pro Max achieves the top-tier IP68 and IP69 dust and water resistance ratings. Second, it also comes standard with an infrared module, so you can use the phone to turn home appliances on and off —it’s very practical for controlling the AC. Also, the X500 Pro Max adopts a dual-sided physical SIM card design. As a Vivo flagship, it naturally includes excellent eSIM support and built-in global roaming services—you get it all, no need to choose. The packaging maintains the Vivo tradition, including a 90W fast charger , a pre-applied screen protector, and a. matching color case. Opening it up... Next, let's look directly at the biggest highlight of the X500 Pro Max: the camera. Since the hardware specs were covered in detail earlier, I'll focus on the key points here. This year's X500 Pro Max features a triple-lens setup, including the previously introduced 50MP 1/1.28-inch Sony LYTIA LYT-910 sensor,. and a 200MP 1/1.4-inch 3.5 x telephoto lens using Samsung HP9. Finally, there is a 50MP 1/2.75-inch ultra-wide-angle lens that doubles as a macro camera. So , on the X500 Pro Max, you can play with both ultra-wide macro and telephoto macro photography. I highly recommend experimenting with telephoto macro; Vivo's telephoto shots are truly impressive. All three lenses support 60FPS autofocus tracking. Finally, let’s shine a bright light on.

it. That's right, Vivo has hidden a multi-zone laser autofocus sensor with 1536 ranging points to the left of the lens module. To give you a more intuitive view of the laser focus, we’ve prepared an infrared camera. As you can see clearly now, when you are shooting, the sensor behind the camera continuously measures distance in real-time, helping the system achieve more stable focus within a certain range . Now, I’ll share three more details about photography. As everyone knows, Vivo has. an incredibly rich set of camera modes, including Landscape, Portrait, Panorama , Stage, Snapshot, Pro, Spatial Camera, and very interesting AI creative tools. With so many fun and useful shooting modes, it’s easy to see why camera enthusiasts love Vivo; it’s highly versatile. Even if you're a photography novice, you can find plenty of enjoyment in the process. When it comes to choosing modes, Vivo’s. design principle is simple: switch to the mode that matches what you’re shooting—use Portrait mode for portraits . Switch to Landscape for scenery, and switch to Stage for performances. Even if you forget, the AI scene recognition will immediately prompt you, "Hey, switching modes will give you better results," which is very thoughtful. In every mode, the system applies the most suitable shooting options. For example, in Stage mode, the system disables distracting settings to improve snapshot performance, allowing you to focus on capturing the performance. And on the. function bar to the right, the system automatically switches to the most suitable options. For instance, in landscape mode, you can quickly select filters and AI styles; it's quite fun to take these interesting AI photos directly, and it automatically switches to 200-megapixel mode to capture more landscape detail. In portrait mode, it automatically switches to various portrait bokeh functions, such as quickly selecting different Zeiss bokeh effects. You can also quickly adjust various beauty settings. Or quickly select portrait. filters, such as the classic CCD, humanistic, Zeiss, or natural styles. And the most important "Qing Tian" collaboration filters are also right here. Second, Vivo has an interesting upgrade this year called 8K Live Photos. We’ve shared this many times: as performance improves and storage grows, I highly recommend everyone start turning on Live Photos for shooting. When you take a photo, the system also records a short video and audio, so you aren't just capturing a photo, but can. return to that moment in time. Especially since life is short; looking back at your pets years later is definitely worth it. This year, Vivo directly provides three Live Photo options: 2K, 4K, and even 8K ultra-high quality. Simply put, it makes the quality of the video captured at the same time much better. However, in 8K, the photo will be cropped to a 16: 9 video aspect ratio. I personally feel that choosing 4K is better; lastly, the X100 Pro Max has macro auto-switching to. ultra-wide lens. In low light, it automatically shows ultra-wide distortion correction, and automatically reduces flare, among other advanced options. What's more unique is that there is a lens defogging function in the camera this time. For example, if you go to a penguin enclosure at the zoo where it's very cold and the lens fogs up, you can activate the defogging function to clear it. Additionally, in the professional photography mode, you can still shoot 50-megapixel RAW, as well as 50-megapixel Super RAW with multi-frame synthesis. All the options needed for professional.

mode are there, so I won't go into detail. Next, let's look at the main battlefield for this year's Android flagships: video recording. First, the biggest update from Vivo is that besides being able to shoot 8K 30fps, they have achieved global 4K 120fps high-frame-rate recording, which naturally supports 4K 120fps slow-motion, perfect for b-roll. But remember, only the main lens can shoot 4K 120fps. Besides that, you can. also record up to 4K 60fps Dolby Vision HDR or 4K 60fps Log video. However, for professional users, I recommend you go directly into the professional video mode found in the Pro series. Here, besides recording at up to 4K 120fps Log , you can also enable AV1 encoding at 4K 60fps to record 10-bit V-Log. Those wanting to shoot cinematic footage can definitely achieve professional-level results. Furthermore, in the top right corner, we can enable real-time monitoring restoration. The system has. built-in Rec.709 and HLG LUT presets, allowing you to quickly restore footage for more accurate monitoring. What's great is that vivo also allows for importing custom LUTs. Additionally, all the essential features for professional video recording are here: startup animations for that ritualistic feel, audio levels, histograms, waveform monitors, focus peaking, and framing guides. They’ve included everything; the feature set is incredibly comprehensive . vivo is truly taking this seriously. By the way, in this mode, you can also switch lenses while recording. However,. if you're a casual user, vivo has added a new option called "Cinematic Workshop ." In this mode, you can enable subject locking, and the system will firmly track your chosen subject. With three framing options—full-body, half-body, and close-up—the system will perform smooth zooms using digital scaling. The most interesting part is that vivo added a "Rotating Camera" setting, allowing you to stand in one spot, press rotate, and capture these highly stylized videos . There are three rotation settings: 90 degrees, 180 degrees, and continuous. loop. There’s also super slow-motion recording at up to 4K 960fps. And dual-lens recording is available as well. In short, vivo's photography features are just too numerous. I’ve tried my best to cover only the highlights, so you'll have plenty to explore once you get your hands on it. One quick tip: if you bought this to film concerts, remember to turn on " Stage Mode," and the system will switch to settings optimized for capturing performances. Even in Stage Mode, you. can still record at up to 4K 60fps in Dolby Vision. I’ll stop here regarding the camera for now. At the end of this video, we’ve also prepared a side-by-side comparison with the latest Find X10 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and S26 Ultra—all the top-tier flagships. Make sure to watch until the end so you don't miss it. Next, let’s look at performance. As a close partner of MediaTek, the vivo X500. Pro Max is certainly a global debut for the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 flagship processor, built on TSMC's N2B process. The version I have here is equipped with 12GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 1TB of storage space. However, since it hasn't been officially released yet, I can't confirm if a 16GB option will be available in Taiwan; we'll have to wait for the official announcement. In addition, this generation uses a larger BCG plate to help with rapid heat dissipation. At this point, we are testing the international hardware version with pre-launch software, so please keep that in mind when evaluating the results.

Let’s jump straight into the performance testing segment. First, let’s look at the CPU performance with Geekbench. Unsure if it is due to the early software, the X 500 ProMax's CPU performance is a bit conservative, scoring 3,738 in single-core and 10,705 in multi-core. Compared to the previous generation Dimensity 9500, it shows about a 12.4%gain in single-core. And about a 10%increase in multi-core, though the peak potential of the Dimensity 9600 likely still has room to be unlocked. As for the GPU, looking at 3DMark Steel Nomad, the X500ProMax. scored 3,540 points. This performance is also about a 10%improvement compared to the 9500. I will skip over the theoretical performance quickly. We will head directly into the game testing segment. First, let's test Genshin Impact. Based on our testing, although the X 500 ProMax's CPU benchmark is a bit conservative, the game optimization is already quite good. After 30 minutes of continuous play at the highest graphics settings in Genshin Impact, it maintained a flat line at an average of 59.96 FPS, completely maxed out. Even the 1%low reached 56.8 FPS, which means. it was smooth throughout the entire session. The highest temperature on the front and back was around 36 degrees, which is excellent thermal control. Next , we tested the more demanding Honkai: Star Rail. After playing for a while at the highest settings, even though the load was clearly heavier, the X500ProMax still held a nearly flat line with an average of 59.81 FPS and a 1%low of 48.7 FPS, which is very, very impressive. However, the front and back temperatures rose to around 42 to 44 degrees. Additionally, the X500ProMax supports bypass charging, allowing you to power the motherboard directly while gaming to reduce heat and extend battery lifespan . Battery life is a major highlight this year; the international version of the vivo X500ProMax uses a large 7800mAh battery. Our testing in forced 120Hz mode resulted in a very impressive 19 hours and 50 minutes. Essentially, you won't have any battery anxiety in daily use. As for charging, the X500ProMax. supports up to 90W wired and 40W wireless fast charging. Based on our tests, the X500ProMax can charge to 50% in half an hour, 97%in one hour, and reaches a full charge in one hour and two minutes; for a large 7800mAh battery , this is very fast. One reminder: if you want to activate the fastest speed, remember to select "High Speed" after plugging it in. Regarding biometrics, the device also hides a very fast ultrasonic fingerprint scanner and includes face unlock. Regarding. communication, the X500 Pro Max's NFC was tested and works with Google Wallet for contactless payments. It supports digital transit cards and common NFC access card functions, and the XO linear motor provides crisp, responsive haptic feedback. Furthermore, the system comes pre-installed with the latest Android 17 and OriginOS 7 operating system. It is worth noting that the vivo X300 Ultra also received the OriginOS 7 update quite quickly, without waiting until the 500 series launch, which is definitely a plus. For connectivity, the X500 Pro Max. features vivo's useful office suite, Vivo Office and Vivo Share, along with the latest Google Quick Share, allowing it to compete with Apple's AirDrop and exchange files with iPhones. There is a big surprise in this update: starting with OriginOS 7, the international version now supports connectivity with the Apple Watch. That's right, you can now use an Apple Watch seamlessly with a vivo phone. Additionally, various useful features are included, such as three-finger swipe for screenshots, three-finger swipe up.

for windows, automatic driving assistance, and the Smart Sidebar. Interestingly, vivo has brought the " Atomic Workbench," previously exclusive to the foldable series, to the X500 Pro Max. Once opened by swiping inward from the bottom right corner, you can see the Atomic Workbench launch. You can open several apps in windows and quickly switch between them using the sidebar on the left. To be honest, the experience is still better on the foldable devices . But at least it provides an extra option for split-screen multitasking. Regarding the AI features everyone cares about, the X500 Pro Max includes Google’s full-screen Circle to Search and Gemini voice assistant, along with gallery tools like AI Eraser for travel photos, AI Super Resolution, AI Expand, and AI color grading. The menu also includes fun, non-AI features like background replacement, artistic filters, and various visual effects. Overall, however, the AI capabilities of the vivo international version are still. growing. Finally, let's look at entertainment; for the X500 Pro Max, vivo opted for a larger 6.85-inch flat display and debuted the BOE Q11 light-emitting material. The real surprise is that this screen has been upgraded to a increasingly rare 2K resolution, supporting a dynamic refresh rate from 1Hz to 144Hz. However, the system mainly operates at a maximum of 120Hz, with. 144Hz available only in select games. Without further ado, let’s jump straight into the actual performance tests. Based on our testing, thanks to the new-gen Q11 material, the X500 Pro Max achieves an excellent 2,250 nits of peak full-screen brightness, reaching a top-tier performance of over 2,000 nits , and hits a peak brightness of 4,400 nits in 10%HDR window tests—the brightness is extremely powerful. Regarding color accuracy, we've once again used our testing equipment, which. represents an investment of over $ 10,000, to perform the analysis. Vivo offers three display modes this time: Natural, Professional, and Bright. We tested all the modes, so let’s get straight to the key takeaways. Based on our tests, the Professional preset is the most accurate. In this mode, the X500 Pro Max achieves 99.2%sRGB coverage , successfully hitting the color gamut target. Regarding color temperature, the X500 Pro Max came in at a CCT deviation of 2.75. However, in the more rigorous. sRGB average color accuracy test, it still delivered an impressive average Delta E of 1.26. A value below 2 is generally considered color-accurate. The maximum Delta E of 3.5 is primarily influenced by the color temperature. Due to system limitations, we were unable to conduct further P3 gamut testing. As for the PWM dimming everyone is concerned about, we used professional equipment to test it. Before that, remember to subscribe to Boni to support us; subscribing is free, but it really means a lot to us. Looking at the results, the. X500 Pro Max does indeed feature 2160Hz high-frequency PWM dimming at low brightness levels. Alright, with testing finished, as usual, it's time for the main event: the new round of flagship comparisons. For this camera test, we've brought in the latest OPPO Find X10 Pro Max, Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the Samsung S26 Ultra for a showdown. We'll start with portrait samples, comparing all phones at their shared focal lengths,.

followed by sharing the X500 Pro Max's 3.5 x portraits. Next, we'll look at the telephoto samples, where we'll first compare the long-range zoom performance, and then provide a comparison of two videos to show the differences for your reference . Come. Moving on to the main lens and ultra-wide lens. Finally, we'll also provide a set of 4K 60FPS video comparisons for your reference. And as a bonus at the very end, we have a set of selfie camera samples. Right. Lastly, regarding audio, the X500 Pro Max also features a dual-speaker configuration,. which we'll mention here. Alright, that's it for this episode. We've covered all the key points within the limited time. If you have any further questions, feel free to leave a comment below. Finally, producing this content is not easy. You're welcome to support us by becoming a channel member or using the "Super Thanks" feature to help us produce more high-quality reviews. Thank you, I'm Lu-Zi. We'll see you in the next video. If you enjoyed this episode, don't forget to subscribe to Boni and turn on notifications so you can receive our latest reviews. Of course, you can also find us on Facebook, Boni's assistant on Instagram , and LINE@.

item.description:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1R52K9CONmo

值得閱讀的理由

  • 瞭解 vivo 最新旗艦 X500 Pro Max 在電池容量與台積電先進製程晶片上的重大規格升級。
  • 掌握首發 Sony LYT-910 感光元件與 17EV 超高動態範圍技術，如何大幅提升影像拍攝品質。
  • 探索全新專業攝影套裝配件、長焦鏡頭下放實力，以及周杰倫聯名「晴天」濾鏡的豐富玩法。

摘要

全新旗艦定位與周杰倫聯名亮點

作者開箱並介紹了 vivo 最新推出的年度旗艦機 vivo X500 Pro Max。本代旗艦最大的話題之一是邀請到 周杰倫 擔任品牌代言人，全系列特別內建了聯名款「晴天」濾鏡以致敬經典 MV 氛圍。核心規格方面，手機搭載採用台積電最新 N2P 製程的天璣 96 Pro 旗艦處理器，電池容量更大幅提升至領先業界的 7,800 mAh，並搭配 90W 有線與 40W 無線快充。

革命性影像規格與專業長焦套裝

影像系統是該機的最大亮點，作者特別點出多項業界領先配置。主鏡頭採用 vivo 與 Sony 聯合研發的 1/1.28 吋 5,000 萬畫素 Sony LYT-910 感光元件，並導入 LOFIC 技術，具備真實 17EV 超高動態範圍，帶來相較一般手機多達 32 倍的動態範圍躍升，並輔以 3 軸 OIS 頂級防手震規格。長焦端則配備 2 億畫素大底潛望鏡頭，並首次下放支援 400mm G2 Ultra 望遠鏡頭 與專業攝影套裝，讓該機無需直上 Ultra 型號就能化身最強「演唱會神器」。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 瞭解 vivo 最新旗艦 X500 Pro Max 在電池容量與台積電先進製程晶片上的重大規格升級。
  • 掌握首發 Sony LYT-910 感光元件與 17EV 超高動態範圍技術，如何大幅提升影像拍攝品質。
  • 探索全新專業攝影套裝配件、長焦鏡頭下放實力，以及周杰倫聯名「晴天」濾鏡的豐富玩法。

摘要

全新旗艦定位與周杰倫聯名亮點

作者開箱並介紹了 vivo 最新推出的年度旗艦機 vivo X500 Pro Max。本代旗艦最大的話題之一是邀請到 周杰倫 擔任品牌代言人，全系列特別內建了聯名款「晴天」濾鏡以致敬經典 MV 氛圍。核心規格方面，手機搭載採用台積電最新 N2P 製程的天璣 96 Pro 旗艦處理器，電池容量更大幅提升至領先業界的 7,800 mAh，並搭配 90W 有線與 40W 無線快充。

革命性影像規格與專業長焦套裝

影像系統是該機的最大亮點，作者特別點出多項業界領先配置。主鏡頭採用 vivo 與 Sony 聯合研發的 1/1.28 吋 5,000 萬畫素 Sony LYT-910 感光元件，並導入 LOFIC 技術，具備真實 17EV 超高動態範圍，帶來相較一般手機多達 32 倍的動態範圍躍升，並輔以 3 軸 OIS 頂級防手震規格。長焦端則配備 2 億畫素大底潛望鏡頭，並首次下放支援 400mm G2 Ultra 望遠鏡頭 與專業攝影套裝，讓該機無需直上 Ultra 型號就能化身最強「演唱會神器」。

質感外觀設計與多元智慧拍照功能

在機身外觀上，作者展示了兼具極簡與細節的「星光灰」配色，背蓋採用具備潮汐起伏微曲弧度的冷雕雙工藝玻璃，支援 IP68 與 IP69 最高防塵防水等級、紅外線遙控以及實體雙卡搭配 eSIM。鏡頭模組旁還隱藏了 1536 測距點的多區雷射對焦感測器以確保穩定對焦。在拍攝體驗上，相機整合了人像、風景與舞台等情境的 AI 自動優化模式，並首創支援高達 8K 動態照片（Live Photos） 與獨特的鏡頭除霧功能，提供全面且豐富的創作樂趣。

================================================

In my hand is the newly released flagship from vivo, the X500 Pro Max. Hi, welcome back. I'm 2027. The new round of flagship smartphone wars has been heating up since October, and right here in my hand is the latest annual flagship from vivo: the X500 Pro Max. The big news this year is that vivo actually got Jay Chou as their brand ambassador. You'll notice not only is he featured in all the early promotional materials, but in the entire X500 series. , vivo has included a co-branded "Sunny Day" filter, recreating the aesthetic of that classic MV, which we'll take a closer look at later. Getting back to it , the vivo X500 Pro Max flagship has all the specs you'd expect, including the new-generation Dimensity 96 Pro flagship processor built on TSMC's latest N2P process. The highlight is that the battery capacity in this international version has been significantly upgraded from the previous generation's 6,510 mAh. to an industry-leading 7,800 mAh, paired with 90W wired and 40W wireless fast charging. However, for those of you watching this for vivo, I’m sure you’re most interested in the camera. Although this year’s X500 Pro Max might look similar to the previous generation on the spec sheet. In reality, the underlying hardware has received a massive overhaul, with many first-time features, especially in imaging. For example, the first industry-first is the new 1/1.28-inch 50-megapixel large sensor co-developed by vivo and Sony. It. utilizes the Sony LYT-L 910 flagship sensor, which features the latest LOFIC technology. With vivo's tuning and the support of LOFIC technology, the X500 Pro Max's main lens can achieve a real 17-stop ultra-high dynamic range. As we’ve shared before, most current smartphones hover around 12EV, and even the previous generation X300 Pro only reached 14EV. So, the 17EV achieved by this LYT-L 910 is 2 to the power of 5 compared to standard 12EV phones, representing a 32-fold improvement. Even. compared to the 14EV of the previous X300 Pro, this generation offers a 2 to the power of 3 improvement, which is an 8-fold increase. According to vivo, the 17EV they claim is a true 17 stops; if using the peak values often cited for marketing, the X500 Pro Max can reach up to 18.4 EV. On top of that, this main lens is also equipped with 3-axis OIS stabilization hardware, achieving a C.0 -level top-tier stabilization spec. Moving past the main lens, let’s look at. the second industry-first: vivo and Samsung have co-launched the new-generation HP0 large-sensor telephoto lens. While it maintains the 1 /1.4-inch 200-megapixel large sensor hardware, it also achieves the C.0- level stabilization spec and adopts a 1 + 5 glass lens design. But the real highlight is this box you see on my table. That's right, today we're unboxing Vivo's top-tier ETB Photography Master Set. Beyond the stylish silver dedicated case, the magnification adapter ring on. it, and the professional photography grip—accessories you're already familiar with—this year's X500 Pro Max directly supports the 200mm Vivo G2 lipstick telephoto lens, as well as the 400mm G2 Ultra telephoto lens, which has been trickled down from the X300 Ultra for the first time. This is also the first time the Pro series has supported the G2 Ultra, letting you turn it into Vivo's best concert-shooting device without needing to step up to the Ultra model. We'll get to that later. By the way,.

this set also includes a strap and two lens rings with different designs that you can swap based on your preference. Finally, seeing the classic ZEISS blue logo on the case, the lens, and the phone itself confirms that the X500 Pro Max continues the deep collaboration between Vivo and ZEISS. Alright, I've talked a bit too much in the intro. As I'm testing this now, I don't know the actual retail price or the version coming to Taiwan yet—you guys can let me know in the comments. Anyway, how does the Vivo X500 Pro Max actually perform? Let's take a look together. Let's start by looking at the exterior. I personally think this year's Vivo X500 Pro Max has become much more refined compared to the simplicity of the previous generation. First, the version we have here is my favorite this year, Starry Gray. From the front, it’s a gray-toned phone with a minimalist design and a high-quality feel. But when you catch it in the light, you. can see the cold-sculpted glass features two sections with different finishes spliced together. Look closer, and you'll see sparkles across the body, just like stars twinkling in the night sky. I actually quite like the name announced at the launch, "Earth Gray," which is very evocative. Besides that, if you look closely at the seam where the sections meet. That's right, the top section is slightly raised. Vivo has cleverly created a curved design on this cold-sculpted glass, inspired by the changing tides. Also, compared to the last generation,. this year’s lens ring features a larger area of dense texturing. Around the Oreo module, there's an added gray border in a matching color. Contrasting with the simplicity of the previous generation, I really like this year's design. By the way, the X500 Pro Max also retains the shortcut button design. So you can do things like long-press to open the camera or double-press to turn on the flashlight; it's a very useful setting. Finally, there are three more points regarding the exterior. First, the X500 Pro Max achieves the top-tier IP68 and IP69 dust and water resistance ratings. Second, it also comes standard with an infrared module, so you can use the phone to turn home appliances on and off —it’s very practical for controlling the AC. Also, the X500 Pro Max adopts a dual-sided physical SIM card design. As a Vivo flagship, it naturally includes excellent eSIM support and built-in global roaming services—you get it all, no need to choose. The packaging maintains the Vivo tradition, including a 90W fast charger , a pre-applied screen protector, and a. matching color case. Opening it up... Next, let's look directly at the biggest highlight of the X500 Pro Max: the camera. Since the hardware specs were covered in detail earlier, I'll focus on the key points here. This year's X500 Pro Max features a triple-lens setup, including the previously introduced 50MP 1/1.28-inch Sony LYTIA LYT-910 sensor,. and a 200MP 1/1.4-inch 3.5 x telephoto lens using Samsung HP9. Finally, there is a 50MP 1/2.75-inch ultra-wide-angle lens that doubles as a macro camera. So , on the X500 Pro Max, you can play with both ultra-wide macro and telephoto macro photography. I highly recommend experimenting with telephoto macro; Vivo's telephoto shots are truly impressive. All three lenses support 60FPS autofocus tracking. Finally, let’s shine a bright light on.

it. That's right, Vivo has hidden a multi-zone laser autofocus sensor with 1536 ranging points to the left of the lens module. To give you a more intuitive view of the laser focus, we’ve prepared an infrared camera. As you can see clearly now, when you are shooting, the sensor behind the camera continuously measures distance in real-time, helping the system achieve more stable focus within a certain range . Now, I’ll share three more details about photography. As everyone knows, Vivo has. an incredibly rich set of camera modes, including Landscape, Portrait, Panorama , Stage, Snapshot, Pro, Spatial Camera, and very interesting AI creative tools. With so many fun and useful shooting modes, it’s easy to see why camera enthusiasts love Vivo; it’s highly versatile. Even if you're a photography novice, you can find plenty of enjoyment in the process. When it comes to choosing modes, Vivo’s. design principle is simple: switch to the mode that matches what you’re shooting—use Portrait mode for portraits . Switch to Landscape for scenery, and switch to Stage for performances. Even if you forget, the AI scene recognition will immediately prompt you, "Hey, switching modes will give you better results," which is very thoughtful. In every mode, the system applies the most suitable shooting options. For example, in Stage mode, the system disables distracting settings to improve snapshot performance, allowing you to focus on capturing the performance. And on the. function bar to the right, the system automatically switches to the most suitable options. For instance, in landscape mode, you can quickly select filters and AI styles; it's quite fun to take these interesting AI photos directly, and it automatically switches to 200-megapixel mode to capture more landscape detail. In portrait mode, it automatically switches to various portrait bokeh functions, such as quickly selecting different Zeiss bokeh effects. You can also quickly adjust various beauty settings. Or quickly select portrait. filters, such as the classic CCD, humanistic, Zeiss, or natural styles. And the most important "Qing Tian" collaboration filters are also right here. Second, Vivo has an interesting upgrade this year called 8K Live Photos. We’ve shared this many times: as performance improves and storage grows, I highly recommend everyone start turning on Live Photos for shooting. When you take a photo, the system also records a short video and audio, so you aren't just capturing a photo, but can. return to that moment in time. Especially since life is short; looking back at your pets years later is definitely worth it. This year, Vivo directly provides three Live Photo options: 2K, 4K, and even 8K ultra-high quality. Simply put, it makes the quality of the video captured at the same time much better. However, in 8K, the photo will be cropped to a 16: 9 video aspect ratio. I personally feel that choosing 4K is better; lastly, the X100 Pro Max has macro auto-switching to. ultra-wide lens. In low light, it automatically shows ultra-wide distortion correction, and automatically reduces flare, among other advanced options. What's more unique is that there is a lens defogging function in the camera this time. For example, if you go to a penguin enclosure at the zoo where it's very cold and the lens fogs up, you can activate the defogging function to clear it. Additionally, in the professional photography mode, you can still shoot 50-megapixel RAW, as well as 50-megapixel Super RAW with multi-frame synthesis. All the options needed for professional.

mode are there, so I won't go into detail. Next, let's look at the main battlefield for this year's Android flagships: video recording. First, the biggest update from Vivo is that besides being able to shoot 8K 30fps, they have achieved global 4K 120fps high-frame-rate recording, which naturally supports 4K 120fps slow-motion, perfect for b-roll. But remember, only the main lens can shoot 4K 120fps. Besides that, you can. also record up to 4K 60fps Dolby Vision HDR or 4K 60fps Log video. However, for professional users, I recommend you go directly into the professional video mode found in the Pro series. Here, besides recording at up to 4K 120fps Log , you can also enable AV1 encoding at 4K 60fps to record 10-bit V-Log. Those wanting to shoot cinematic footage can definitely achieve professional-level results. Furthermore, in the top right corner, we can enable real-time monitoring restoration. The system has. built-in Rec.709 and HLG LUT presets, allowing you to quickly restore footage for more accurate monitoring. What's great is that vivo also allows for importing custom LUTs. Additionally, all the essential features for professional video recording are here: startup animations for that ritualistic feel, audio levels, histograms, waveform monitors, focus peaking, and framing guides. They’ve included everything; the feature set is incredibly comprehensive . vivo is truly taking this seriously. By the way, in this mode, you can also switch lenses while recording. However,. if you're a casual user, vivo has added a new option called "Cinematic Workshop ." In this mode, you can enable subject locking, and the system will firmly track your chosen subject. With three framing options—full-body, half-body, and close-up—the system will perform smooth zooms using digital scaling. The most interesting part is that vivo added a "Rotating Camera" setting, allowing you to stand in one spot, press rotate, and capture these highly stylized videos . There are three rotation settings: 90 degrees, 180 degrees, and continuous. loop. There’s also super slow-motion recording at up to 4K 960fps. And dual-lens recording is available as well. In short, vivo's photography features are just too numerous. I’ve tried my best to cover only the highlights, so you'll have plenty to explore once you get your hands on it. One quick tip: if you bought this to film concerts, remember to turn on " Stage Mode," and the system will switch to settings optimized for capturing performances. Even in Stage Mode, you. can still record at up to 4K 60fps in Dolby Vision. I’ll stop here regarding the camera for now. At the end of this video, we’ve also prepared a side-by-side comparison with the latest Find X10 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and S26 Ultra—all the top-tier flagships. Make sure to watch until the end so you don't miss it. Next, let’s look at performance. As a close partner of MediaTek, the vivo X500. Pro Max is certainly a global debut for the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 flagship processor, built on TSMC's N2B process. The version I have here is equipped with 12GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 1TB of storage space. However, since it hasn't been officially released yet, I can't confirm if a 16GB option will be available in Taiwan; we'll have to wait for the official announcement. In addition, this generation uses a larger BCG plate to help with rapid heat dissipation. At this point, we are testing the international hardware version with pre-launch software, so please keep that in mind when evaluating the results.

Let’s jump straight into the performance testing segment. First, let’s look at the CPU performance with Geekbench. Unsure if it is due to the early software, the X 500 ProMax's CPU performance is a bit conservative, scoring 3,738 in single-core and 10,705 in multi-core. Compared to the previous generation Dimensity 9500, it shows about a 12.4%gain in single-core. And about a 10%increase in multi-core, though the peak potential of the Dimensity 9600 likely still has room to be unlocked. As for the GPU, looking at 3DMark Steel Nomad, the X500ProMax. scored 3,540 points. This performance is also about a 10%improvement compared to the 9500. I will skip over the theoretical performance quickly. We will head directly into the game testing segment. First, let's test Genshin Impact. Based on our testing, although the X 500 ProMax's CPU benchmark is a bit conservative, the game optimization is already quite good. After 30 minutes of continuous play at the highest graphics settings in Genshin Impact, it maintained a flat line at an average of 59.96 FPS, completely maxed out. Even the 1%low reached 56.8 FPS, which means. it was smooth throughout the entire session. The highest temperature on the front and back was around 36 degrees, which is excellent thermal control. Next , we tested the more demanding Honkai: Star Rail. After playing for a while at the highest settings, even though the load was clearly heavier, the X500ProMax still held a nearly flat line with an average of 59.81 FPS and a 1%low of 48.7 FPS, which is very, very impressive. However, the front and back temperatures rose to around 42 to 44 degrees. Additionally, the X500ProMax supports bypass charging, allowing you to power the motherboard directly while gaming to reduce heat and extend battery lifespan . Battery life is a major highlight this year; the international version of the vivo X500ProMax uses a large 7800mAh battery. Our testing in forced 120Hz mode resulted in a very impressive 19 hours and 50 minutes. Essentially, you won't have any battery anxiety in daily use. As for charging, the X500ProMax. supports up to 90W wired and 40W wireless fast charging. Based on our tests, the X500ProMax can charge to 50% in half an hour, 97%in one hour, and reaches a full charge in one hour and two minutes; for a large 7800mAh battery , this is very fast. One reminder: if you want to activate the fastest speed, remember to select "High Speed" after plugging it in. Regarding biometrics, the device also hides a very fast ultrasonic fingerprint scanner and includes face unlock. Regarding. communication, the X500 Pro Max's NFC was tested and works with Google Wallet for contactless payments. It supports digital transit cards and common NFC access card functions, and the XO linear motor provides crisp, responsive haptic feedback. Furthermore, the system comes pre-installed with the latest Android 17 and OriginOS 7 operating system. It is worth noting that the vivo X300 Ultra also received the OriginOS 7 update quite quickly, without waiting until the 500 series launch, which is definitely a plus. For connectivity, the X500 Pro Max. features vivo's useful office suite, Vivo Office and Vivo Share, along with the latest Google Quick Share, allowing it to compete with Apple's AirDrop and exchange files with iPhones. There is a big surprise in this update: starting with OriginOS 7, the international version now supports connectivity with the Apple Watch. That's right, you can now use an Apple Watch seamlessly with a vivo phone. Additionally, various useful features are included, such as three-finger swipe for screenshots, three-finger swipe up.

for windows, automatic driving assistance, and the Smart Sidebar. Interestingly, vivo has brought the " Atomic Workbench," previously exclusive to the foldable series, to the X500 Pro Max. Once opened by swiping inward from the bottom right corner, you can see the Atomic Workbench launch. You can open several apps in windows and quickly switch between them using the sidebar on the left. To be honest, the experience is still better on the foldable devices . But at least it provides an extra option for split-screen multitasking. Regarding the AI features everyone cares about, the X500 Pro Max includes Google’s full-screen Circle to Search and Gemini voice assistant, along with gallery tools like AI Eraser for travel photos, AI Super Resolution, AI Expand, and AI color grading. The menu also includes fun, non-AI features like background replacement, artistic filters, and various visual effects. Overall, however, the AI capabilities of the vivo international version are still. growing. Finally, let's look at entertainment; for the X500 Pro Max, vivo opted for a larger 6.85-inch flat display and debuted the BOE Q11 light-emitting material. The real surprise is that this screen has been upgraded to a increasingly rare 2K resolution, supporting a dynamic refresh rate from 1Hz to 144Hz. However, the system mainly operates at a maximum of 120Hz, with. 144Hz available only in select games. Without further ado, let’s jump straight into the actual performance tests. Based on our testing, thanks to the new-gen Q11 material, the X500 Pro Max achieves an excellent 2,250 nits of peak full-screen brightness, reaching a top-tier performance of over 2,000 nits , and hits a peak brightness of 4,400 nits in 10%HDR window tests—the brightness is extremely powerful. Regarding color accuracy, we've once again used our testing equipment, which. represents an investment of over $ 10,000, to perform the analysis. Vivo offers three display modes this time: Natural, Professional, and Bright. We tested all the modes, so let’s get straight to the key takeaways. Based on our tests, the Professional preset is the most accurate. In this mode, the X500 Pro Max achieves 99.2%sRGB coverage , successfully hitting the color gamut target. Regarding color temperature, the X500 Pro Max came in at a CCT deviation of 2.75. However, in the more rigorous. sRGB average color accuracy test, it still delivered an impressive average Delta E of 1.26. A value below 2 is generally considered color-accurate. The maximum Delta E of 3.5 is primarily influenced by the color temperature. Due to system limitations, we were unable to conduct further P3 gamut testing. As for the PWM dimming everyone is concerned about, we used professional equipment to test it. Before that, remember to subscribe to Boni to support us; subscribing is free, but it really means a lot to us. Looking at the results, the. X500 Pro Max does indeed feature 2160Hz high-frequency PWM dimming at low brightness levels. Alright, with testing finished, as usual, it's time for the main event: the new round of flagship comparisons. For this camera test, we've brought in the latest OPPO Find X10 Pro Max, Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the Samsung S26 Ultra for a showdown. We'll start with portrait samples, comparing all phones at their shared focal lengths,.

followed by sharing the X500 Pro Max's 3.5 x portraits. Next, we'll look at the telephoto samples, where we'll first compare the long-range zoom performance, and then provide a comparison of two videos to show the differences for your reference . Come. Moving on to the main lens and ultra-wide lens. Finally, we'll also provide a set of 4K 60FPS video comparisons for your reference. And as a bonus at the very end, we have a set of selfie camera samples. Right. Lastly, regarding audio, the X500 Pro Max also features a dual-speaker configuration,. which we'll mention here. Alright, that's it for this episode. We've covered all the key points within the limited time. If you have any further questions, feel free to leave a comment below. Finally, producing this content is not easy. You're welcome to support us by becoming a channel member or using the "Super Thanks" feature to help us produce more high-quality reviews. Thank you, I'm Lu-Zi. We'll see you in the next video. If you enjoyed this episode, don't forget to subscribe to Boni and turn on notifications so you can receive our latest reviews. Of course, you can also find us on Facebook, Boni's assistant on Instagram , and LINE@.

item.itunes:author: 邦尼幫你 3C 科技 - 開箱評測
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aL3wWyJmwWo

值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解滾筒拖地機器人如何邊拖邊清潔滾筒，並改善醬料、寵物腳印等髒污的清理效果。
  • 掌握 Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Flow 的主要升級，包括薄型機身、吸力提升、第二代滾筒拖布與高溫自清潔。
  • 認識 AI 視覺辨識、避障、地毯防濕及防纏毛設計等實用功能，評估它是否適合居家清潔需求。

摘要

滾筒拖布與新一代機身

Donkey 以蠔油清潔示範比較雙圓盤拖布與滾筒拖布：傳統拖布往往得反覆清洗才能處理大面積髒污，而滾筒能在拖地時持續自我清潔，因而更有機會一次清除醬料、寵物腳印與地板污漬。Roborock 推出的 Qrevo Edge 2 Flow，則把新一代滾筒拖地系統與更纖薄的機身結合。

升級版滾筒拖地系統

新機改用可升降 LDS 定位模組，機身高度從前代約 11.9 公分縮減至 8.98 公分，有助於進入低矮家具下方；即使 LDS 降下，機身前方的定位視窗仍可協助辨識環境。吸力也從前代 20,000Pa 提高至 35,000Pa。

拖地部分升級為第二代 SpiraFlow 2.0 滾筒系統：機身內加入加壓供水，出水口從 8 個增加至 16 個，使長達 27 公分的滾筒能更均勻補水。柔性刮水結構則有助於刮除污水、控制水量並減少拖後水痕；污水回收設計也能將固體髒污隔離，降低系統堵塞機率。污水盒取消多餘凹槽與濾網，滾筒可一鍵拆卸，支架亦可抬起清潔，維護更方便。

貼邊清潔、避障與智慧策略

滾筒下壓力最高達 15N，並可伸出最多 4.4 公分進行貼邊清潔；遇到地毯時，系統會抬起滾筒並降下滾筒護罩，隔開濕區與乾區。機器人搭載單線結構光、邊緣感測器與 RGB AI 視覺模組，可辨識超過 280 種障礙物，前置補光燈則讓它在較暗環境中仍能辨識物品。

例如辨識到充電線時，機器人會在地圖標示並提前避開；遇到地上的醬油，則會抬起側刷與主刷、關閉風扇，只用滾筒拖布深度清潔，之後先返回基座清洗再繼續工作。它也支援窗簾清潔策略，以及暫時略過被人或寵物擋住的區域、稍後再回頭補掃；寵物用品區則可開啟加強清潔。

防纏毛設計與基座維護

底部採用防纏繞萬向輪、雙懸臂主刷與長短弧形側刷等設計。主刷中央留有空隙，讓毛髮在清掃時往中間集中並落入集塵盒；安裝時須保留中央空隙，才能發揮最佳效果。側刷碰到邊緣時會高速反轉，試圖將角落碎屑帶出。電池容量為 5,400mAh，實際續航則留待後續測試。

基座具備自動集塵、補水、污水收集與除臭模組，但沒有內建清潔劑模組，使用者須依指定比例自行將清潔劑加入水箱。機器人回站清洗滾筒時，系統會以最高 75°C 熱水沖洗，並透過加壓出水口清潔；多數污水會被回收到基座污水箱，減少滾筒浸泡在髒水中的情形。清洗後再以 63°C 熱風烘乾；今年的斜坡與底盤也可拆下沖洗。

後續實測預告

Donkey 表示，產品功能介紹告一段落後，影片將進行 15 項嚴格測試，完整呈現實測過程與優缺點；不過目前提供的內容尚未包含測試結果。Donkey 也提到，Roborock 清潔機器人社群成員已超過 66,000 人。

================================================

Traditional dual-disc mops can only spread oyster sauce evenly and cannot handle it. But Roborock's latest high-end roller mop handles even oyster sauce with ease. That 's right, Roborock has finally brought us their new generation of high-end roller mops, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow! Hi, welcome back, I'm Donkey. Friends who want to clean their floors are certainly familiar with roller mops. As our opening demonstration clearly showed,. traditional dual-disc mops can only handle large areas of dirt by repeatedly rinsing the mop. But with a roller mop, even a whole oyster sauce can be cleaned in one go with ease. However, cleaning oyster sauce isn't the key point. The most important aspect of a roller mop is that it cleans itself while mopping, allowing it to clean even a whole oyster sauce in one pass. Not to mention, when cleaning your floor, the roller is constantly self-cleaning , better handling. advanced scenarios like pet paw odor and floor stains. This is why Roborock generated so much discussion in Bonnie's robot community when they launched their first roller mop, the Qrevo Curv 2 Flow, in 2026. Nowadays, if you want a truly thorough cleaning , you should prioritize a robotic vacuum cleaner. The biggest highlight of the newly launched Qrevo Edge 2 Flow this year is that Roborock has eliminated the protruding LDS positioning module. and replaced it with a new generation of lifting LDS. This has drastically reduced the Edge 2 Flow's overall thickness from nearly 12 cm (11.9 cm) in the previous generation to less than 9 cm (only 8.98 cm ), making it the thinnest front-loading robotic vacuum cleaner in Taiwan. This is definitely good news for those who need to clean low furniture. Incidentally, to accommodate the lifting LDS design, Roborock has also added a positioning window at the front of the robot. So even after the LDS module is lowered, the robot can still detect the environment about 100 degrees in front of it. through the small front window to continue positioning in low-ceilinged spaces. Those who don't want to use the lifting function can also turn it off in the app. But that's not all. Next, as usual, we 'll summarize the Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Flow for you. The main highlights are : First, the suction power of the Roborock vacuum module has been further increased from 20,000Pa in the previous generation to 35,000Pa, meeting the high-end standard of 2026. We'll see the actual performance in real-world testing later. For.

mopping, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow has been upgraded to Roborock's second-generation SpiraFlow 2.0 roller washing system. There are three major changes: First, Roborock's second- generation roller wash has added a pressurized module inside the body. Compared to previous roller wash models that could only replenish water through dripping , the second-generation roller module can now pressurize , providing a more stable and even supply of clean water to the roller. Importantly, it's not just about pressurization. ; Roborock has also doubled the original 8 water outlets to 16 pressurized water outlets. These two upgrades are significant for this 27cm long... For a roller mop, the evenness of water replenishment is significantly improved , and the self-cleaning effect of the roller itself is also enhanced. In addition, Roborock also uses a flexible wastewater recycling squeegee module. This slight elasticity not only allows the squeegee to fit more closely to the roller and scrape off dirt, but also, more importantly , it can achieve more stable water control. and reduce water stains after mopping. Speaking of which, Roborock's wastewater filtration is quite good . The squeegee itself is integrated with a whole water guide channel, so all solid dirt is blocked outside the filter screen and will not clog the entire wastewater recycling system due to small objects getting stuck. You just need to remember to take out the filter strip and the wastewater box at the rear of the car regularly for a rinse. It is worth mentioning that Roborock has improved the design of the wastewater box this time. They have removed unnecessary grooves and filters , and the top cover can be pulled out completely. , making it easier to clean. In terms of maintenance, the roller can be removed with one click, and the bracket module can also be lifted for easier cleaning. Overall, the entire logic of the Roborock 2nd generation is obviously more mature, the water output evenness has been improved, and the wastewater recycling system is easier to maintain . It has indeed brought the roller mop series back to the high-end track in 2026. In terms of floor cleaning efficiency, this roller has been further upgraded to a higher 240. It also boasts a powerful 15N downward pressure. to thoroughly clean dirt from the floor. Furthermore, as a high-end roller from Roborock, it features a telescopic edge-cleaning design. When the robot detects an object's edge, the roller can extend up to 4.4cm for edge-cleaning. But that's not all; the essential 15mm roller lift and roller shield hardware for high-end rollers are also present in the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow. So, as you can see in the video, when the robot encounters a carpet, the system automatically lifts the roller module and lowers the built-in roller shield,.

physically separating wet and dry areas. Okay, now that we've covered Roborock's second-generation roller, let's continue. First, in terms of the main positioning solution , the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow uses a lifting LDS module for rapid spatial detection , lowering the body to 8.98cm. Regarding obstacle avoidance hardware , we can see through the infrared camera that Roborock uses a single-line structured light module on the front for rapid obstacle detection , while the sides have edge sensors. for edge-sensing. In addition, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow also features Roborock's signature AI... The RGB visual recognition module can recognize over 280 types of obstacles , and it also has a built-in fill light at the front , so the visual module can continue to recognize obstacles even in low light . For example, when the AI ​​recognizes a charging cable, it will mark the cable on the map , and the robot will choose to avoid it from a distance. By the way, this lens also supports classic Roborock functions such as video calls and pet capture. However, compared to video calls, the greatest value of this lens is that it allows the robot to see the real world and then intelligently adjust its cleaning strategy . For example, when the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow sees a puddle of soy sauce on the floor, the AI ​​will immediately raise the two side brushes, raise the main brush , and turn off the fan. Next, use only the roller mop for deep cleaning to prevent the robot from getting soy sauce on it . After cleaning heavily soiled areas, the robot will immediately go home to wash itself before continuing to clean. Not only that, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow. also supports curtain cleaning strategies and a very practical pet/human obstruction cleaning feature. For example, when the robot is cleaning, it may be blocked by children or pets, so it will temporarily abandon that area and clean other places first , then return to clean up the missed spots later. Additionally, pet owners can enable the deep cleaning option for pet supplies , which will automatically enhance the cleaning of that area. Next, we flip the Qrevo Edge 2 over. The Flow also uses Roborock's signature three-anti-tangle design,. including anti-tangle omnidirectional wheels and anti-tangle dual cantilever brushes. The principle is to leave a gap in the middle of the main brush; during cleaning, hair automatically gathers towards the center and eventually falls off and is collected in the dustbin, achieving physical anti-tangle. The only thing to note is that when installing the main brush, remember to leave a gap in the middle for optimal anti-tangle performance. Finally, Roborock also uses two sets of long and short curved anti-tangle side brushes, allowing hair to fall off naturally during rotation.

Interestingly, these side brushes automatically reverse at high speed when touching edges , trying to sweep up debris from corners and improving edge-touching performance. In terms of battery life, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow uses a 5400mAh battery; we will test its actual performance later. Finally, we see the base station section of the Qrevo Edge 2. The Flow also features built-in automatic dust collection, automatic water tank replenishment , a wastewater tank, and a deodorization module to reduce wastewater odor. However, this generation does not have a built-in detergent module. ; users can add detergent directly to the water tank according to the specified ratio . The biggest change this time is that the Roborock also adopts a wastewater separation self-cleaning design. When the robot comes home to clean the drum, the system directly injects high-temperature water (up to 75 degrees Celsius) into the body and cleans the drum through 16 new pressurized water outlets. Importantly, most of the dirty water is directly recycled into the wastewater tank and pumped back to the base station's wastewater tank, reducing the problem of the drum being soaked in dirty water for self-cleaning. This is also the approach for the new generation of drums in 2026. After cleaning the drum, the system uses 63-degree hot air to dry it. And there's good news: compared to the previous generation , this year's Qrevo Edge 2 Flow... The ramp and chassis can be disassembled for cleaning. For pet owners, simply rinse it under the tap – quick, effective, and efficient . I'll stop here for now , but to truly appreciate its power, we'll put it to the test . In today's episode, we'll conduct 15 rigorous tests,. recording the entire process. The results are right before your eyes, highlighting both advantages and disadvantages. By the way, the Bonnie Helps You Sweep and Mop Robot community has officially surpassed (updated) 66,000 members! There are many genuine user shares and discussions. Thank you for participating! Whether you're considering buying, have already bought, or not , scan the QR code to join the Taiwan Sweeping Robot discussion forum , or check the information section or pinned comment for the link. Let's start with the design. This year's Qrevo Edge 2 Flow features a mainstream round body design , with both the main unit and base station in a simple and durable all-white color scheme, easily blending into any home. However, note that the glossy cover is relatively easy to scratch; those concerned should take note. For mopping, this generation offers 30 water volume settings. However, what's special about this model is that we can adjust the water volume via the app... Selecting the smart water volume adjustment function will allow the system to use visual recognition at the front of the machine to adjust the appropriate water volume.

based on the floor material , controlling water streaks . If you still want to adjust it manually, the rules remain the same: start with the lowest setting, test if it's not enough, and gradually increase the setting to avoid water streaks. Unless you have pets, the roller will smell after washing, indicating insufficient water volume. As we've said many times, the cleanliness of the roller is completely linked to the water volume. If there are any issues with cleaning, first increase the mopping water volume and switch the base station to a 10-minute soaking high-temperature wash to ensure the roller is clean. , but this will require more water. In addition, if you have hardwood floors, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow also has a built-in cleaning function that moves along the floor direction, reducing friction in the crevices. As a high-end product from Roborock, this model also supports the Hello Rocky voice assistant; all voice commands can be viewed in the app. Roborock also supports the Matter protocol and can connect to Google Home, Google Assistant , Alexa, and Siri. Okay, now. that the key points are covered , let's move on to our new 15 In the first test of the practical application , we prepared three common household cleaning hazard items: 10 grams each of cookie crumbs, sunflower seed shells , and red beans, totaling 30 grams. These represented small, long , and round, heavier items, allowing us to observe the robot's cleaning performance and whether the side brushes would scatter the red beans. The test began, and we observed that the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow, with its intelligent cleaning strategy activated,. automatically increased suction power and used a cross-grid cleaning method when encountering large areas of dirt. However, the dual side brush design still resulted in some red beans being scattered, but fortunately, they were all recovered during subsequent cleaning. After the test, we weighed the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow. Originally 30g , the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow recovered 29.80g, achieving a recovery rate of 99.3%. This performance firmly places it among the top performers. The second test was a corner cleaning test. We again controlled 10g of cookie crumbs and evenly distributed them in a corner. The test began. As you can see, when approaching the corner, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow's side brushes automatically reversed, trying to reach the edge as deeply as possible . Our actual measurement showed that the original 10g... Of the cookie crumbs recovered, 8.07g was recycled , representing a recovery rate of 80.7%. According to the database, the cleaning efficiency is about 60% without extension brushes and about 80% to 85% with extension brushes.

Therefore, the side brush reversal does indeed contribute to cleaning. For the third test, we measured the cleaning time. We also compiled all the test results into a table for easier viewing . Our tests showed that the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow can complete cleaning in about 4 minutes, regardless of whether the lights are on or off. Compared to the current high-end models that clean in about 5 minutes, this is a very fast performance. For the fourth test, the hair entanglement test, we directly measured the length of the long hair set at 70-80cm. and filled the test space with 1 gram of hair. Test started, test ended. This is a test that Roborock excels at. The hair was successfully separated without entanglement by the dual-arm brushes and the left and right side brushes . For the fifth test, the obstacle test, we first tested its performance with the lights on. As you can see from the image,. it successfully identified and avoided potentially hazardous items such as charging cables, extension cords, and pet poop on the floor. A small detail is that when the Qrevo Edge 2... When Flow passes near high-risk obstacles, you'll see it raise its little hands to handle them as cautiously as possible. If there's no risk of the robot getting stuck, it will boldly approach or even push away the obstacle to clean, conforming to mainstream cleaning strategies. The system also successfully cleans around circular or cylindrical objects. . If you're a more cautious user , you can set a less-collision mode in the app, where the robot will choose a more conservative strategy for obstacle avoidance. In the sixth level , we'll test it again with the lights off . For those who like to see infrared images, this is also a good time to observe how the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow's sensing module works. The results are basically the same as with the lights on , and thanks to the supplementary lighting, visual recognition continues even with the lights off. It definitely avoids obstacles. However, I still want to remind everyone to pick up larger pieces of trash before cleaning, open the doors used for map creation , and tidy up wires and other debris . My conclusion from testing so many robots is that no matter how advanced , it's impossible to clean without tidying up. So, tidying up is still necessary. In the seventh level, we'll test its mopping performance. Here 's a little tip: for small areas of dirt, you can use the app... Select the area you want to mop,.

and the app will show the floor cleaning option. This allows for small-area mopping , but be careful with roller mops. I've said many times that I recommend sweeping first, then mopping, or at most sweeping and mopping simultaneously . Never mop a large area at once. In pure mopping mode, the system raises the main brush and side brushes, then uses only the 27cm roller to mop. Even a large area of ​​oyster sauce is no problem for a roller mop . However, I still want to remind everyone that this test is mainly to verify the roller's effectiveness. If you often have this kind of situation at home, I suggest using the floor cleaner we tested earlier, as it's more practical. The eighth test is the noise test. Here's the table: The Qrevo Edge 2 Flow has five suction modes in pure sweeping mode. In silent mode, it's only 59 dB , but for daily use, standard or the third level is sufficient. I've said countless times that for most households, running it to the maximum won't get much cleaner , but it will damage the battery. The ninth test is the battery life . Our new robot test uses a unified standard; it can complete 23 consecutive cleaning cycles in the same space. The tenth test is the charging test. The Qrevo Edge 2 Flow takes approximately 2 hours and 50 seconds to charge from 15% . A full charge in minutes is sufficient compared to the typical four to five hours for a robot vacuum and mop, and around three hours for a high-end model . If the battery is low, the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow also has a resume cleaning function; the robot will quickly return home to recharge before cleaning the remaining areas. For the eleventh test, the roller cleaning, we went straight to the "devil's challenge" —immersing the roller entirely in a mixture of soy sauce and soy paste. Here's the before and after picture of the clean roller . Next, we used the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow's new self-cleaning system at a high temperature of up to 75 degrees Celsius. The results are clear from the image: the roller was thoroughly cleaned. For the twelfth test, the base station dust collection,. we used 30g of mixed debris plus a half-filled bag of dog hair to collect dust. The Qrevo Edge 2 Flow's dust collection performance was also excellent. For the thirteenth test, the carpet test , our tests showed that when the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow encountered a short-pile carpet.

, the rear roller module automatically raised by 15mm , and the roller cover automatically lowered, achieving dry and wet separation . For the long-haired section, the same method applies without any problems. For those with carpets, you can enable the "Carpet First, Carpet Pressure Increase , Carpet Second Cleaning " options in the app . The robot will then sweep the carpet first when the drum is completely dry , automatically increasing suction power and using a cross-grid cleaning method. for a more thorough cleaning. If you bought it specifically for carpets or have large carpets or long-haired carpets, I highly recommend the Saros 20. It's arguably the Roborock flagship with the most comprehensive carpet cleaning strategy currently available. Finally, for the fourteenth obstacle test, Roborock officially states a 2cm threshold, so we tested a 2cm threshold without issue . If your threshold is a bit low , you can slightly raise it with a mat. or use a robot-specific threshold assist pad. In the final test, we tested the robot's ability to overcome the IKEA recliner obstacle. The test footage shows no obstacle getting stuck. Test OK! All fifteen tests completed. Overall, the upgrades to the Qrevo Edge 2 Flow are noticeable, including the replacement with a 35000Pa high-powered fan,. more in line with the 2026 flagship performance, and the second-generation drum cleaning module, achieving increased pressure and an upgrade to 16... The holes allow for more even water distribution , and the lifting LDS achieves a slim 8.98cm design. Combined with Roborock's already comprehensive smart cleaning strategy , those waiting for Roborock's slim roller should not be disappointed. As for the base station... Including essential features for high-end models like automatic water replenishment, automatic dust collection, 75-degree high-temperature cleaning with pressurization and self-cleaning , and a 63-degree hot air drying function. , it has everything you 'd expect . My only personal preference is the automatic detergent dispensing function , which would make it truly complete. Finally, I'm hoping that Roborock's first flagship drum floor cleaner will be released soon! Okay, that's all for this episode. We tried our best to test as much as possible within the limited time. If you have any questions , feel free to leave a comment below to discuss them. I'm Donkey, and see you next time!
